newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares flat, market eyes Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares flat, market eyes Wall Street.

text.p: Norwegian shares spent another session mainly flat on Wednesday and dealers said that with many investors out, the market would take a lead from Wall Street.

The Total share index slipped 0.26 percent to close at 1,236.08 points. The market touched an intraday high at 1,240.15 points, but failed to break into new record territory following the recent run of 14 consecutive all-time peaks.
Turnover totalled 1.68 billion crowns, of which power producer Hafslund accounted for 675 million crowns.
Sweden's Vattenfall sold 13,658,200 Hafslund shares to Norwegian subsidiary Vattenfall Norge AS.
The transfer represents 11.8 percent of Hafslund's total equity and 20 percent of the voting rights in the company.
Also heavily traded was conglomerate Orkla, which retreated five crowns to 577 crowns in turnover of 171 million crowns after hitting an intraday low at 570 crowns.

Dealers said it was unclear why interest in Orkla was relatively high, although the stock was attractive at the lower levels. "Maybe people are disappointed that nothing has come of the rumors about PepsiCo," said one dealer. Last week Orkla rose strongly on expectations that it would sign a production deal with PepsiCo.
